hub.note: Canonical programme, standing context, and evidence-backed memory substrate.

jobs.description: Claims get attacked before they get believed.
jobs.human_control: A human owns what ships under the company’s name. Verification reduces the risk; it never transfers the accountability.
jobs.replacement_claim: The confident wrong number that makes it into the proposal, the deck, or the deal. One bad claim repeated to a client costs more credibility than a hundred verified ones earn.
jobs.note: Exact evidence matching, source hashing, privacy boundaries, secret scanning, path containment, unsupported-reference rejection and draft-only authority are enforced with negative controls; human publication accountability remains explicit.

jobs.description: Test agent outputs against a benchmark before they touch real work.
jobs.replacement_claim: The blind trust that an agent still works after you changed its prompt · until a client catches the regression for you.
jobs.note: A repeatable with-skill/without-skill evaluation and benchmark surface exists.

jobs.description: Per-client context files stay current as work happens.
jobs.replacement_claim: The “wait, what’s the latest with this client?” tax every time anyone touches an account.
jobs.note: Librarian protocol and automatic daily capture provide a durable maintenance loop.

jobs.description: Webinar and talk decks in the brand design system.
jobs.replacement_claim: 6–10 hours per webinar deck, or $500–1,500 to a designer who needs the content anyway · meaning you do the thinking twice.
jobs.note: The evidence-linked outline now renders as an editable six-slide PPTX with claim-bound speaker notes, A1 draft authority, deterministic overflow testing, per-slide render hashes and full-size visual QA.

jobs.description: Any question → structured, cited report with diagrams.
jobs.replacement_claim: $2–5k boutique research engagements, or the decision made without one.
jobs.note: A deterministic compiler now renders a structured cited report with a Mermaid evidence-flow diagram, source hashes, exact line spans, QA gates and a committed trust-kernel receipt.

jobs.description: Turn delivered work into reusable playbooks.
jobs.replacement_claim: The expertise that walks out the door with whoever did the work. Every delivered project contains a repeatable playbook · and without this node, you rebuild it from scratch the next time, at full cost, forever.
jobs.note: Repeated approved successful runs compile into a source-hashed draft SOP only when every step has two independent run receipts; path escape, evidence tamper, inconsistent steps and implicit release fail closed. Release requires a separate named operator receipt.

jobs.description: Every meeting becomes searchable, structured context.
jobs.replacement_claim: Meetings that evaporate. Every client call contains decisions, commitments, and context worth money · and in most firms it lives nowhere but two people’s fading memory of a Tuesday.
jobs.note: Local transcripts compile into source-hashed action, decision, question and learning-gap candidates; every item retains exact line evidence and remains draft-only until a separate named operator approval receipt is issued.

jobs.description: Find and rank candidates for open roles across platforms.
jobs.replacement_claim: A recruiter’s 20–25% placement fee, or 10+ founder-hours per role scrolling profiles · which is why most small companies hire from whoever happened to apply.
jobs.note: Owned by the independent Market Aligner/JAA product and linked rather than absorbed.

jobs.description: Score every lead against ICP so outreach spends effort where it converts.
jobs.replacement_claim: Reps spending identical effort on a perfect-fit account and a tire-kicker, because the list doesn’t know the difference. Effort allocation is the multiplier on everything downstream.
jobs.note: Owned by the independent Market Aligner/JAA product.

jobs.description: Watch every automation for failures and silent stalls · know before the client does.
jobs.replacement_claim: Finding out an automation died three days ago because a client asked where their report is.
jobs.note: A deterministic read-only collector now observes declared cross-service event and file heartbeats, detects silent stalls, dead processes, malformed sources and unavailable paths, and feeds active-agent and queue-state evidence into the operator-status contract without executing configured commands. The live 22 Jul packet correctly reports the stopped orchestrator and stale Jarvis heartbeat as degraded. Monitoring remains partial because the Integration Builds prerequisite is still only documented.

jobs.description: Scheduling, conflicts, buffers, and timezone math handled.
jobs.replacement_claim: A part-time EA’s core duty ($15–25k/year), or the founder doing timezone math at midnight and the double-booking that torches a first impression.
jobs.blocker: No live calendar connector is installed and authorised.

jobs.description: The inbox sorted by what actually needs the human.
jobs.human_control: Triage is autonomous; sending is not. Replies go out after a human approves · and the agent never deletes, only archives, so a misjudged email is a search away, not gone.
jobs.replacement_claim: The 1–2 hours a day a founder spends in the inbox, of which maybe fifteen minutes is decisions and the rest is sorting other people’s priorities.
jobs.blocker: No live email connector is installed and authorised.

jobs.description: Record, transcribe, and file every meeting automatically.
jobs.human_control: Humans run the meeting; the system just never forgets it. Flag sensitive calls as do-not-record · the convention matters more than the tool.
jobs.replacement_claim: Notes that don’t exist, decisions nobody wrote down, and “wait, what did we agree?”
jobs.note: The local transcribe skill is installed; universal recording, consent capture, and automatic filing are not yet implemented.

jobs.description: Financials, growth signals, org structure, strategic posture.
jobs.replacement_claim: A junior analyst day ($300–500 equivalent) per company researched properly · so it only happens for deals already in motion, when it should happen before.
jobs.note: The installed account-research skill is available; no general giga-user workflow is yet evidenced.

jobs.description: Turn a pile of research into charts and diagrams that explain themselves.
jobs.replacement_claim: The research that lands as a wall of text nobody reads · or the analyst who spends an afternoon making one chart.
jobs.note: Installed visualization and spreadsheet capabilities are available but not integrated as one workflow.

jobs.description: Brand-consistent images from reference libraries.
jobs.replacement_claim: Stock photos that look like stock photos, or $50–200/image from a designer for routine brand visuals.
jobs.note: The installed image generation skill is available but not a deployed giga-user workflow.

jobs.description: Background, content trail, interests, mutual ground for any contact.
jobs.replacement_claim: Walking into rooms not knowing who you’re talking to.
jobs.note: The installed account-research skill is available; no general giga-user workflow is yet evidenced.

jobs.description: Chase and verify every credential and API key needed to build.
jobs.human_control: Credentials are handled by a named human into a proper secrets store · never pasted into chat, never stored in the agent’s context. The agent chases and verifies; it does not hold the keys.
jobs.replacement_claim: The 1–2 weeks of “still waiting on that API key” that delays every build start · the single most common cause of week-one slippage, and it bills nobody.

jobs.description: Layer firmographics, tech stack, and headcount trends onto target accounts.
jobs.replacement_claim: The research step everyone skips: outreach to a company you don’t understand reads like spam because it is.

jobs.description: Watch a target list for funding, hiring, leadership, and tech changes · ongoing.
jobs.replacement_claim: Finding out a target raised, hired a VP, or switched tools weeks late · from their newsletter, not your radar.

jobs.description: Generate and iterate paid-ad variations · hooks, angles, formats.
jobs.replacement_claim: The creative bottleneck on every paid account · one ad, no variations, fatiguing while you sleep.

jobs.description: Turn your happiest customers into referrals, reviews, and case studies.
jobs.replacement_claim: The case studies and referrals you never ask for · happy clients who would gladly help if anyone caught the moment.

jobs.description: Produce the services agreement the moment a deal closes verbally.
jobs.human_control: A lawyer blesses the master template once; a human reviews every generated agreement before it goes out. AI fills and adapts · it never invents a clause.
jobs.replacement_claim: The 3–10 day gap between “yes” and paperwork, where verbal closes go to die. Plus $300–800 of lawyer time per agreement if you draft each one fresh instead of templating once.

jobs.description: The signals that matter reach the right person · the noise gets filtered.
jobs.replacement_claim: The monitoring that becomes noise · 200 alerts a day, all ignored within a week.

jobs.description: Brand-safe formatted docs for sponsor sign-off.
jobs.replacement_claim: Script versions scattered across email threads and chat, plus 30–60 minutes per deal of formatting · multiplied by every revision round the mess itself creates.

jobs.description: Mine comments and DMs for questions, objections, and content ideas.
jobs.replacement_claim: Reading comments for dopamine instead of data. Your audience tells you exactly what to make next, every day, in writing · and almost nobody logs it.

jobs.description: Spend vs budget by category, with overruns flagged early.
jobs.replacement_claim: The budget set once in January and never looked at again · overruns discovered at tax time.

jobs.description: Who actually decides · economic buyer, champion, blockers, their roles.
jobs.human_control: A human runs the deal · this draws the board so they know who to win and in what order. Enterprise deals are lost to unmapped committees more than to bad pitches.
jobs.replacement_claim: The deals that stall because you were selling to the wrong person · no map of who actually signs.

jobs.description: Keep records deduped, fields normalized, stages honest.
jobs.replacement_claim: The 10–20% of records that are duplicates, dead, or wrong · and every report, forecast, and automation silently built on top of them. Garbage hygiene taxes every node downstream.

jobs.description: Deals, contacts, and statuses stay current everywhere.
jobs.human_control: Merges and deletions get a human click. A bad sync that creates a duplicate is annoying; one that destroys a record is archaeology.
jobs.replacement_claim: The gap between what the CRM says and what’s actually true · which quietly invalidates every report, forecast, and reactivation play built on top of it.

jobs.description: Push finished campaigns into sending platforms with correct settings.
jobs.human_control: A human reviews the rendered test send before volume flows. Launch is the last gate where a broken token costs nothing · one minute of eyes here versus 2,000 apologies later.
jobs.replacement_claim: The hour of fiddly platform setup per campaign · and the occasional disaster where the {firstName} token goes out raw to the whole list.

jobs.description: Build multi-channel cadences · email, LinkedIn, phone touches in order.
jobs.replacement_claim: Single-channel outbound. Email-only gets email-only results · coordinated email, LinkedIn, and phone touches lift reply rates 2–3×, but sequencing them by hand across hundreds of leads is a planning job nobody sustains.

jobs.description: Platform-correct captions with CTA placement rules baked in.
jobs.replacement_claim: The 20 minutes per post that happens after the creative energy is spent · which is why most captions are an afterthought stapled to good content.

jobs.description: Design and export branded carousel slides.
jobs.replacement_claim: $100–300 per carousel from a designer with a 3-day turnaround, or 2–4 hours of founder time per set fighting a drag-and-drop tool.

jobs.description: Project cash in and out · know your runway before it becomes an emergency.
jobs.human_control: A human owns the assumptions and the calls that follow · this does the math, fast and honestly, and shows its work. The decisions stay human.
jobs.replacement_claim: The fractional CFO’s headline deliverable · or, more often, no forecast at all and a founder guessing at runway.

jobs.description: Predict which accounts are about to slip · before the usage even dips.
jobs.replacement_claim: The renewal that surprises you by not happening · the exit interview that should’ve been a save three weeks earlier.

jobs.description: Cut long recordings into short-form clips worth posting.
jobs.replacement_claim: $1–2k/month clipping agencies, or an editor billing hours to watch footage. A one-hour webinar holds 5–10 postable clips that mostly die unwatched in a recordings folder.

jobs.description: Write multi-step cold email sequences tuned to the vertical and offer.
jobs.human_control: A human approves every new sequence before launch and owns the offer it sells. Once a sequence is proven, AI varies it within the approved frame.
jobs.replacement_claim: A $60–80k/year SDR’s core output · or a $2–4k/month agency retainer that sends the same template to everyone.

jobs.description: Call and voicemail scripts with branching objection handling that read human.
jobs.human_control: A human delivers it · this drafts the words, the rep makes them sound like a person. The objection branches are the value, not the opener.
jobs.replacement_claim: The reps who freeze on the call because nobody wrote the branches · or the "script" that’s one paragraph and dies at the first objection.

jobs.description: Overdue invoices get chased politely and persistently.
jobs.human_control: Tone escalation past the second nudge gets a human decision · the relationship is worth more than the invoice.
jobs.replacement_claim: The awkwardness of chasing money · which is why founders chase late and lose weeks of cash flow to their own politeness.

jobs.description: Detect keyword comments on content and deliver the promised asset by DM.
jobs.replacement_claim: Manually DMing a link to 400 commenters · which means either hours of phone time after every post that pops, or broken promises to the exact people who raised their hands.

jobs.description: Scrape and transcribe competitor content; extract hook patterns.
jobs.replacement_claim: Watching competitors casually instead of systematically. Their viral posts are free R&D · someone else paid the testing cost.

jobs.description: Pricing, positioning, strengths, weaknesses, exploitable gaps.
jobs.replacement_claim: Competing on guesswork. Most firms can’t articulate a competitor’s pricing or positioning beyond adjectives.

jobs.description: Find and append emails, phones, and LinkedIn profiles to every lead.
jobs.replacement_claim: A list you can’t reach. Without enrichment, 40–60% of a raw list has no usable contact · paying for leads and reaching half of them is the silent tax on every campaign.

jobs.description: Renewals, expiries, and obligations tracked so nothing sneaks up.
jobs.replacement_claim: The auto-renewal you forgot to cancel · the client contract that lapsed because nobody tracked the date.

jobs.description: Token and API spend tracked against budget · no surprise bills.
jobs.replacement_claim: The surprise five-figure API bill · token spend nobody was watching until accounting flagged it.

jobs.description: One idea → native formats for every platform.
jobs.replacement_claim: The 5× content multiplier everyone talks about and almost nobody operationalizes, because manual repurposing is genuinely tedious.

jobs.description: Move and clean data between systems without losing or mangling a row.
jobs.replacement_claim: The migration project that quotes at $5–20k and still loses rows · or the intern hand-copying records between two CRMs for a fortnight.

jobs.description: Pull targeted company and contact lists from structured databases.
jobs.human_control: A human sets the target and spot-checks 10 rows per pull. Bad lists poison everything downstream · the check takes five minutes and saves a campaign.
jobs.replacement_claim: 4–6 hours/week of an SDR pulling and cleaning lists · roughly $8–12k/year of a $65k rep’s time spent not selling.

jobs.description: Spin up tracked, password-gated deal rooms per prospect.
jobs.replacement_claim: PDF proposals that get forwarded into the void. A tracked room tells you who opened what, when · intel a PDF can never give you.

jobs.description: Sponsored scripts in the proven format, per brand brief.
jobs.human_control: Two approvals, both human: the sponsor signs off on claims, and the creator approves every line spoken under their name. Never let an agent invent a capability claim for someone else’s product · fact-check before it goes on camera.
jobs.replacement_claim: Days of back-and-forth per sponsored script, with revision cycles quietly eating the deal’s margin. A $5k brand deal at four revision rounds is a $2k brand deal.

jobs.description: Keep domains healthy · warmup, spam testing, inbox rotation.
jobs.replacement_claim: The silent campaign killer. Everything upstream can be perfect and none of it matters from spam · and most teams find out a month of wasted sends too late.

jobs.description: Turn discovery notes into a working visual prototype before the next meeting.
jobs.human_control: AI builds the prototype; the human decides whether it ships. Nothing reaches a prospect without the seller’s eyes on it.
jobs.replacement_claim: The two-week proposal gap where deals go cold. A visual prototype sent same-day collapses the “is this possible?” conversation entirely.

jobs.description: High-volume structured extraction from client documents.
jobs.human_control: Humans review the low-confidence queue and own the gold-standard set. The machine earns autonomy field by field, measured against it.
jobs.replacement_claim: Teams of people reading documents and retyping them into systems. At volume this is entire payrolls · the densest ROI node on this map for document-heavy businesses.

jobs.description: Every document named, filed, and findable in ten seconds.
jobs.replacement_claim: The Friday afternoon spent hunting for "the signed SOW from March" · multiplied across everyone, every week.

jobs.description: Validate every address before it ever gets a send.
jobs.replacement_claim: Domain burn. A 5% bounce rate doesn’t cost you 5% of sends · it gets the domain flagged, and the next 10,000 emails land in spam.

jobs.description: Every member question and mention gets a response in the house voice.
jobs.replacement_claim: A community manager’s core hours · or the slow death where member questions sit unanswered for two days and the space quietly becomes a noticeboard.

jobs.description: Filings and obligations per entity, tracked and scheduled.
jobs.human_control: Filings get signed by a human, full stop. AI tracks, prepares, and nags · it never submits anything with legal weight on its own.
jobs.replacement_claim: Missed filings, and what they cost: late penalties, a suspended entity, or a frozen bank account discovered the week you need it. Multi-entity founders carry a deadline list nobody actually maintains.

jobs.description: Spot the angry, the churn-risk, and the edge case · and get a human there fast.
jobs.human_control: An angry customer never gets a bot. The system’s entire job is detection and speed · the conversation that follows is a human’s, with full context in hand.
jobs.replacement_claim: The churn you find out about in a one-star review. By the time a frustrated customer asks for a manager, they’ve usually been simmering across three polite tickets nobody connected.

jobs.description: Run the AMAs, calls, and spotlights on a cadence the community can count on.
jobs.replacement_claim: The community that goes quiet because the AMAs and calls stopped happening · running events is a part-time job nobody owns.

jobs.description: Spend categorized for the accountant before they ask.
jobs.human_control: Tax treatment is judgment, not classification · deductibility calls and anything the accountant would raise an eyebrow at stay human.
jobs.replacement_claim: $150–400/month of bookkeeper categorization, or the annual shoebox week where the founder relives twelve months of receipts to answer the accountant’s spreadsheet.

jobs.description: Answer the questions that repeat · and turn them into living help content.
jobs.human_control: A human reviews new auto-drafted articles before they publish, and owns the escalation line the moment an answer isn’t in the corpus.
jobs.replacement_claim: The 40–60% of support volume that is the same fifteen questions, answered by hand, forever.

jobs.description: Draft the recap email with next steps before the prospect forgets the call.
jobs.replacement_claim: The recap email that goes out two days late or never. Deals lose momentum in the gap between the call and the follow-up · and the gap is usually just the seller being busy.

jobs.description: Probability-weight the pipeline into a revenue forecast.
jobs.human_control: The model weights the pipeline; the deal owner adjusts the calls. A human who just left the room knows things no stage-probability ever will · the forecast is a draft until someone accountable signs it.
jobs.replacement_claim: Revenue surprises in both directions. The founder’s number is usually hope-weighted, not probability-weighted · and the gap between them is the months of runway you didn’t know you were missing.

jobs.description: Rounds, investors, revenue estimates, filings · who just got budget.
jobs.replacement_claim: The 30-minute dig through Crunchbase, news, and filings to answer "do they actually have budget" · done for every account, by hand.

jobs.description: Tracking against the income target, with pace forecasts.
jobs.replacement_claim: Discovering in November that the year’s number was never going to happen.

jobs.description: Answer staff policy questions from the real handbook · leave, expenses, onboarding admin.
jobs.human_control: Anything legal, sensitive, or about comp/termination escalates to a human immediately · this answers the routine 80% from documented policy and never invents one.
jobs.replacement_claim: The first HR hire a small team can’t justify yet · and the founder fielding "how much leave do I have" between sales calls.

jobs.description: Clean documentation when a system ships to the client.
jobs.replacement_claim: The post-handoff support tail: every undocumented system generates months of “quick questions” that are really unpaid retainer work. Bad handoffs also quietly cap your referrals · nobody recommends a system they can’t operate.

jobs.description: Score every account on usage, sentiment, and engagement · before renewal season.
jobs.human_control: The score surfaces risk; a human makes the call. No automated message ever goes to an at-risk account without an owner deciding to send it.
jobs.replacement_claim: Finding out an account was at risk in the cancellation email.

jobs.description: Generate and rank hooks per platform from proven patterns.
jobs.replacement_claim: The blank-page tax on every piece of content. The hook is 80% of performance and the part most creators spend the least time on.

jobs.description: Route interested replies to the calendar and the pipeline instantly.
jobs.replacement_claim: The hours an interested reply sits in an inbox while the prospect cools. Interest decays by the hour · a hot reply answered next morning converts at a fraction of one answered in minutes.

jobs.description: Define and refine ideal customer profiles per vertical · firmographics, pain patterns, buying triggers.
jobs.human_control: The founder owns this forever. AI drafts and refreshes; the human decides who the business is for. Never fully delegated.
jobs.replacement_claim: The founder’s gut feel, applied inconsistently by everyone downstream. Bad ICP wastes every dollar spent after it.

jobs.description: Sort inbound email and DMs · client, lead, brand deal, noise.
jobs.replacement_claim: The founder as a human sorting machine · 60–90 minutes a day deciding what each message even is before any real work starts, with the important ones buried under the noise.

jobs.description: When an automation breaks · triage, root-cause, fix, and write the note.
jobs.replacement_claim: The frantic hour of "what broke and why" every time an automation falls over · usually during a client deliverable.

jobs.description: Wire client systems together · CRMs, calendars, transcripts, payments.
jobs.replacement_claim: The core billable work of an automation practice · and the part where scope creeps silently. Done by hand, each integration is days of reading API docs, handling auth, and discovering the vendor’s documentation lied.

jobs.description: Branded invoices per entity, currency, and tax treatment.
jobs.human_control: A human glances at every invoice over a threshold before it sends. Money out the door wrong costs more than the glance.
jobs.replacement_claim: The founder doing invoices on Sunday night, occasionally wrong, across entities and currencies.

jobs.description: Welcome email, access checklist, and project scaffold the day a deal closes.
jobs.human_control: The delivery lead sends the welcome email under their own name and owns the kickoff date it promises. The pack assembles itself; the commitment is human.
jobs.replacement_claim: The 3–5 day dead zone between signature and first real work · the window where buyer’s remorse lives. Plus 2–3 hours of assembling the same welcome email, checklist, and folder structure for every new client.

jobs.description: Conversion copy for the whole page · hero, proof, offer, FAQ, CTA.
jobs.replacement_claim: A $2–5k copywriter per page, or worse · the founder writing feature lists nobody converts on.

jobs.description: Parse intake forms and score inbound leads before a human looks.
jobs.human_control: AI scores and sorts; a human owns where the disqualification line sits and audits the auto-declines. Spotting the bad-fit lead that’s secretly a strategic exception stays a judgment call.
jobs.replacement_claim: 30–45 minutes of discovery call per lead that should never have been booked. Unqualified calls are the most expensive way to learn someone has no budget.

jobs.description: Turn content themes into gated guides and landing pages.
jobs.replacement_claim: The “we should make a guide” task that stays on the roadmap for two quarters.

jobs.description: Draft connection notes and DM sequences that read human.
jobs.human_control: Messages send under a real person’s name · that person reads what goes out under it. Approval per sequence, not per message.
jobs.replacement_claim: The 30 connection requests/day a founder sends in a good week and zero in a busy one. Consistency is the entire channel.

jobs.description: Merge, dedupe, and segment raw leads into campaign-ready lists.
jobs.replacement_claim: The 2–3 hours per campaign of merging CSVs and fighting duplicates · and the reputational cost when the same CEO gets the same email from two of your sequences.

jobs.description: Build new target lists off the shape of your closed-won accounts.
jobs.replacement_claim: The expansion list nobody builds methodically · most teams guess at "who else looks like our best clients" instead of extracting the actual pattern.

jobs.description: Turn the tickets that repeat into canned, on-brand responses agents reuse.
jobs.replacement_claim: Every agent re-typing the same answer from scratch · and answering it slightly differently each time.

jobs.description: Map the total addressable companies in a target vertical before a campaign.
jobs.replacement_claim: Guessing how big the pond is. Teams campaign into verticals without knowing whether the addressable universe is 400 companies or 40,000 · and misprice the effort either way.

jobs.description: Propose slots, book calls, chase no-shows.
jobs.human_control: The calendar owner sets the rules once · buffers, hours, who qualifies. The agent never negotiates exceptions; humans do.
jobs.replacement_claim: The 4–7 message back-and-forth that kills deal momentum, plus the no-shows nobody chases.

jobs.description: Client call transcripts → action items → assigned and tracked.
jobs.human_control: The delivery lead confirms owners and deadlines before the recap goes to the client · commitments are made by people.
jobs.replacement_claim: Action items agreed on a client call that evaporate by Thursday · the quiet killer of delivery trust.

jobs.description: Find and celebrate member wins · the retention engine.
jobs.replacement_claim: The retention engine nobody runs because it’s nobody’s job: member wins scroll past unnoticed, and the people most likely to renew never get told they matter.

jobs.description: Keep the space clean · spam, conduct, and noise handled quietly.
jobs.human_control: Spam removal automates clean. Conduct calls don’t · warning or removing a real member is a judgment a human makes, with the receipts the system gathered.
jobs.replacement_claim: The founder deleting crypto spam at 7am, and the slower cost: one unchecked bad actor or pile-on thread can empty a community faster than any feature can fill it.

jobs.description: Who knows whom · paths into a target account.
jobs.human_control: The map is AI’s; the ask is yours. Spending relationship capital · who to ask, for what, when · is judgment no agent should exercise, because the cost of a clumsy ask lands on a human relationship.
jobs.replacement_claim: Cold outreach to accounts where a warm path already existed. A warm intro converts at multiples of cold · and most founders can’t name their second-degree reach into any given target.

jobs.description: Every mention of your brand, competitors, and topics · as it lands.
jobs.replacement_claim: A $200/mo media-monitoring tool, plus the gap it leaves on competitor and topic coverage.

jobs.description: Design and send the weekly email in the brand system.
jobs.replacement_claim: 3–5 hours/week of writing and formatting, or $500–1k/month to a ghostwriter · and the issue that quietly skips a week, then two, then the list goes cold.

jobs.description: Every page ships with share-ready open-graph imagery.
jobs.replacement_claim: Links that unfurl as a blank gray rectangle in every DM, Slack, and LinkedIn share. Each naked link is a small credibility tax, paid on the exact surface where your content travels.

jobs.description: Mine every call for the objections that come up · build the rebuttals that win.
jobs.replacement_claim: The objection-handling knowledge that lives only in the head of your best closer · and walks out the door when they do.

jobs.description: Draft responses to common objections from a tuned library.
jobs.human_control: The library is human-authored from real won deals · AI retrieves and adapts, it never invents a new counter-argument that no one has tested live.
jobs.replacement_claim: Re-improvising the same five rebuttals forever. Every outbound motion gets the same objections · price, timing, “we have someone”, “send info” · and most reps answer each one slightly worse than last time.

jobs.description: New hires get the playbooks, access, and 30-day plan automatically.
jobs.replacement_claim: The new hire’s lost first month · asking around for access, absorbing context by osmosis · and the senior person’s week spent re-explaining what should have been written down.

jobs.description: Guide every new customer through activation, step by step.
jobs.replacement_claim: 2–4 CSM hours per new account sending the same welcome sequence by hand · or the silent version, where customers who stall in week one become the churn stat of month three.

jobs.description: Know what’s paid, due, and late · without opening a bank app.
jobs.replacement_claim: The weekly bank-app archaeology session · logging into three accounts across two currencies to reconstruct who’s paid. Plus the invoice you forgot was unpaid until the quarter closed.

jobs.description: Rank your own content corpus · what worked, what to re-hash.
jobs.replacement_claim: Posting on instinct while your own corpus already knows what works. Your top 10 posts are a content strategy · if anything reads them.

jobs.description: Build a personalization dossier per prospect · hooks, context, common ground.
jobs.replacement_claim: 10–15 minutes per prospect done properly · which is why nobody does it properly past the first twenty.

jobs.description: Weekly pipeline state · what moved, what stalled, what closes next.
jobs.replacement_claim: The Monday hour of assembling pipeline state by hand · or the more common alternative, running the business on whatever the founder remembers the pipeline looking like.

jobs.description: Spin up client-scoped delivery portals with live status.
jobs.replacement_claim: The “can you send me an update?” email and the status deck rebuilt before every check-in call · 2–3 hours/week per active client of pure performance theatre.

jobs.description: Session summaries and deliverables flow into the client portal automatically.
jobs.replacement_claim: The gap between work done and work visible. Without it, the portal decays into a brochure within two weeks and you’re back to manually updating two places · the work and the story about the work.

jobs.description: Extract outcomes, action items, and deal updates from the transcript.
jobs.human_control: The deal owner skims the extracted actions same-day · 2 minutes to confirm what a human promised another human.
jobs.replacement_claim: 30 minutes of post-call admin per meeting that either eats selling time or doesn’t happen.

jobs.description: Build a brief before every call · who, company, history, objectives, talking points.
jobs.replacement_claim: The 20 scrambled minutes before every call · or worse, walking in cold and asking questions the website answers.

jobs.description: What the market charges, anchors, and packaging patterns.
jobs.replacement_claim: Pricing by mimicry or by nerve. Most firms set prices once, from two competitor pages and a feeling, and leave 20–40% of margin on the table for years.

jobs.description: Model anchors, phase structures, and ROI comparisons per deal.
jobs.human_control: AI models the structures; the human picks the number. Price is positioning, leverage, and read-of-the-room · the final figure on every deal is a human call, never a model output.
jobs.replacement_claim: Pricing by gut and anchoring low under pressure. The hour of FTE-comparison math and phase-structuring that justifies a 2–3× higher number · done properly for big deals, skipped for the rest.

jobs.description: Stand up the repo, context files, and plan for a new engagement.
jobs.replacement_claim: The half-day of setup before any real work starts · repo, context files, folder conventions, plan doc · done slightly differently every time, so no two projects are navigable the same way.

jobs.description: Match the right case study to each prospect’s industry and problem.
jobs.replacement_claim: Sending the SaaS case study to the manufacturer. Generic proof reads like no proof · relevance is what makes evidence land, and matching it by hand is one more step nobody does at volume.

jobs.description: Generate branded proposals rendered to PDF from call context.
jobs.human_control: AI drafts structure and prose; a human owns scope and price on every proposal. Those two numbers are never delegated.
jobs.replacement_claim: 3–6 hours per proposal · and for services firms doing tenders, often 2–3 days per response. This is frequently the bottleneck on revenue itself.

jobs.description: Schedule and post across platforms via API.
jobs.human_control: A human eyeballs account, caption, and asset before each scheduled batch goes live. A wrong-account post is a screenshot forever · the two-minute check is non-negotiable.
jobs.replacement_claim: The daily posting chore that survives exactly until the first busy week. Inconsistency is the silent killer of every content flywheel · the algorithm forgets faster than you recover.

jobs.description: Verify every build against real data before the client sees it.
jobs.human_control: A human signs off before anything is shown to a client · the agent runs the checks, but the name on the engagement owns the standard. QA sign-off is never delegated to the thing being QA’d.
jobs.replacement_claim: The bug the client finds before you do. Every defect that reaches a client costs more trust than ten caught internally · and rework eats 10–20% of delivery hours at firms that ship on vibes.

jobs.description: Build the quarterly business review from real account data.
jobs.replacement_claim: 3–5 CSM hours per account per quarter assembling slides from scattered data · which is why most QBRs are either skipped or improvised from memory in the parking lot.

jobs.description: Revive dormant deals and win back lost ones on a schedule.
jobs.human_control: A human approves the revival list monthly · some dead deals should stay dead, and only a human knows which.
jobs.replacement_claim: The revenue sitting in your dead-deals column. Most pipelines have 6 figures of “went quiet” that nobody systematically revisits.

jobs.description: Spot the "talk to my colleague" replies and action the warm intro.
jobs.replacement_claim: The warm intros that evaporate · a prospect says "talk to my colleague in ops" and the reply sits unactioned for a week until the moment’s gone.

jobs.description: Time renewal conversations and spot upsell openings.
jobs.human_control: Renewal and upsell conversations are human, full stop. AI decides when and arms the talker · timing, account history, the expansion angle. The ask itself never automates.
jobs.replacement_claim: Renewals discovered two weeks out and handled in a panic, plus the expansion revenue nobody asked for because nobody noticed the account had outgrown its plan.

jobs.description: Read every reply and tag it · interested, objection, referral, not now, never.
jobs.human_control: Edge cases route to a human within minutes; everything else is logged for a weekly 15-minute audit of the classifier’s calls.
jobs.replacement_claim: The inbox-checking anxiety loop. At volume, a human misses hot replies for 6+ hours · and speed-to-reply is the highest-leverage variable in outbound.

jobs.description: Monthly revenue truth across entities and currencies.
jobs.replacement_claim: Either $200–500/month of bookkeeper time assembling a report that arrives three weeks stale, or the founder rebuilding the same spreadsheet every month and trusting it less each time.

jobs.description: Make the site legible to search engines and LLMs.
jobs.replacement_claim: $1–3k/month SEO retainers that mostly produce reports · or being invisible to the growing share of buyers who ask an LLM for a recommendation instead of searching.

jobs.description: First-pass screens and interview logistics, handled.
jobs.human_control: AI filters; humans reject and advance. Every no on a real candidate is a human call · a person’s livelihood deserves more than a threshold, and so does your reputation in a small market.
jobs.replacement_claim: The 30 minutes per applicant a first-pass screen actually takes, multiplied by the 80% who were never going to make it · plus the scheduling ping-pong that loses good candidates to faster companies.

jobs.description: Full reel and video scripts in the house voice.
jobs.replacement_claim: 2–3 hours per script done properly, or $150–500 per script from a freelancer who doesn’t sound like you. At a daily posting cadence that’s a part-time hire.

jobs.description: Schedule sends by timezone and pace volume to protect reply rates.
jobs.replacement_claim: Blasting everyone at 9am your time · including the prospects for whom that’s 2am, and the inbox providers for whom that spike looks exactly like spam.

jobs.description: Harvest engaged audiences · post commenters, followers, group members.
jobs.replacement_claim: The list nobody builds by hand: everyone who engaged with a competitor’s post is a warm prospect, but scraping them manually takes hours per post.

jobs.description: Acknowledge and engage every inbound lead within minutes.
jobs.replacement_claim: The two days between a form fill and a founder’s reply. Inbound leads contacted within five minutes convert at multiples of those contacted next-day · and most businesses are measured in days.

jobs.description: Clients see progress without asking for it.
jobs.human_control: Good news can ship on autopilot; bad news cannot. A human delivers every delay or problem personally before it appears in writing.
jobs.replacement_claim: The update email that takes 30 minutes to write per client per week · or doesn’t get written, which is how clients conclude nothing is happening. Silence reads as stalling even when the work is flying.

jobs.description: How many companies actually fit · the real size of the prize.
jobs.replacement_claim: The board-deck number pulled from thin air · or a $15k analyst engagement to size a market.

jobs.description: What a target company runs, and where the gaps are.
jobs.replacement_claim: Pitching an integration to a company that can’t run it · or missing the account whose stack is screaming for what you sell. Manual stack-checking is 15–20 minutes per company across detection tools, job posts, and page source, so it happens for almost none of them.

jobs.description: Scroll-stopping thumbnails and covers tuned to earn the click.
jobs.replacement_claim: The click you lose before anyone reads a word · most content dies on a weak thumbnail, not weak content.

jobs.description: Classify, prioritize, and route every support request the moment it lands.
jobs.replacement_claim: The first hour of every support shift · a rep reading, labeling, and forwarding before anyone gets helped. Misrouted tickets bounce between owners 2–3 times and add a day per bounce.

jobs.description: Watch the niche for breaking topics and rising formats.
jobs.replacement_claim: An hour a day of feed-scrolling disguised as research.

jobs.description: Watch for buying signals · hiring, funding, tech changes, leadership moves.
jobs.replacement_claim: Outreach timed by your calendar instead of theirs. The gap between a 2% and a 10% reply rate is often just catching a company the week something changed.

jobs.description: Is this vertical worth entering · demand, budgets, buying behavior.
jobs.replacement_claim: Entering a vertical on one good anecdote · then discovering six months in that the budgets were never there. A proper market assessment runs $5–15k from a research firm, so most firms skip it and pay in wasted quarters instead.

jobs.description: Programmatic video · overlays, captions, motion graphics on recordings.
jobs.replacement_claim: $50–150 per reel to an editor with a 2–5 day turnaround · and the turnaround is the real cost, because trend content dies waiting in someone’s queue.

jobs.description: Personalized video scripts · the hook, the personal line, the CTA, under 90 seconds.
jobs.replacement_claim: 10+ minutes per personalized video done right · which is why reps record three then quit.

jobs.description: The shortest real intro path into a target account · who can connect you.
jobs.replacement_claim: The cold open you didn’t need to send · a warm intro path existed and nobody looked for it.

jobs.description: Scrape local businesses, directories, and niche sources for leads.
jobs.replacement_claim: The lists databases don’t sell · local businesses, niche directories, marketplaces. Built by hand this is days of copy-paste per territory, so it simply doesn’t get built.

jobs.description: Tag why deals close or die; feed patterns back into targeting.
jobs.human_control: The losing seller writes the first draft of why · then someone who wasn’t in the deal reads it skeptically. Self-reported loss reasons are where pipelines lie to themselves most fluently.
jobs.replacement_claim: Paying full tuition for every lost deal and keeping none of the lesson. Most teams can’t say why their last five losses died beyond “price” · which is almost never the real reason.
